name: Comparison and Contrast
blurb: Hơn kém, tương đồng, khác biệt

words.definitionEn: to be unlike or distinct in nature, form, or characteristics
words.example: The two theories differ significantly in their approach to economic development.

words.definitionEn: the state or quality of being similar; resemblance
words.example: There is a striking similarity between the two paintings despite their different periods.

words.definitionEn: the state of being noticeably different from something else when compared
words.example: The contrast between urban and rural lifestyles is becoming more pronounced.

words.definitionEn: able to be compared; similar in quality or quantity
words.example: The salaries in the two sectors are not directly comparable due to different benefit packages.

words.definitionEn: equal in value, amount, function, or meaning
words.example: A bachelor's degree in one country is often equivalent to a master's degree in another.

words.definitionEn: a great difference between things
words.example: The growing economic disparity between the rich and the poor is a major concern.

words.definitionEn: comparable in certain respects, typically in a way that makes clearer the nature of the things compared
words.example: The human heart is analogous to a pump in its function.

words.definitionEn: to have a mutual relationship or connection, in which one thing affects or depends on another
words.example: Income levels correlate strongly with educational attainment in most societies.

words.definitionEn: a difference or contrast between similar things or people
words.example: The distinction between formal and informal learning environments is often blurred.

words.definitionEn: the process or state of diverging; a difference in opinions, interests, or trends
words.example: There has been a noticeable divergence in the economic policies of the two countries.

words.definitionEn: occurring or existing at the same time or in a similar way; corresponding
words.example: The development of digital technology runs parallel to the rise of the internet.

words.definitionEn: a person or thing that corresponds to or has the same function as another person or thing in a different place or situation
words.example: The British Prime Minister met with his French counterpart to discuss trade.

words.definitionEn: belonging or relating separately to each of the people or things previously mentioned
words.example: The two companies reported their respective profits for the fiscal year.

words.definitionEn: corresponding in size or amount to something else
words.example: The amount of tax paid is proportional to the income earned.

words.definitionEn: a mutual relationship or connection between two or more things
words.example: There is a strong correlation between exercise and mental health.

words.definitionEn: a subtle difference in meaning, opinion, or attitude
words.example: The nuance between the two policies is often overlooked by casual observers.

words.definitionEn: consisting of parts or people that are similar to each other or of the same type
words.example: A homogeneous society may lack the cultural diversity found in multicultural nations.

words.definitionEn: consisting of parts or people that are very different from each other
words.example: The city's population is highly heterogeneous, comprising many ethnicities.

words.meaningVi: đặt cạnh nhau để so sánh
words.definitionEn: to place close together or side by side for comparison or contrast
words.example: The author juxtaposes traditional values with modern technology to highlight their conflict.

words.definitionEn: to be similar or in agreement with something; to evoke a feeling of shared experience
words.example: The themes of the novel resonate with the struggles of contemporary society.

words.definitionEn: not able to exist or be true at the same time
words.example: Economic growth and environmental protection are not mutually exclusive if managed properly.

words.definitionEn: in a way that is opposite in direction, effect, or order
words.example: The price of a product is inversely related to its supply.

words.definitionEn: to depart from an established course or standard
words.example: The results of the experiment deviate significantly from the initial hypothesis.

words.definitionEn: a division or contrast between two things that are represented as being opposed or entirely different
words.example: The dichotomy between mind and body has been debated for centuries.

words.definitionEn: the state of being equal, especially in status, value, or power
words.example: The treaty aims to achieve parity in military spending between the two nations.

words.definitionEn: to be similar or look like someone or something
words.example: The two theories resemble each other in their fundamental assumptions.

words.definitionEn: exactly the same in every way
words.example: The results of the experiment were identical to those obtained previously.

words.definitionEn: clearly different or separate
words.example: These two issues are distinct and should be treated separately.

words.definitionEn: to recognize or show the difference between things
words.example: It is crucial to differentiate between correlation and causation.

words.meaningVi: sự khác biệt, không nhất quán
words.definitionEn: a difference between two or more things that should be the same
words.example: There is a significant discrepancy between the two sets of data.

words.definitionEn: to be in opposition or disagreement with something
words.example: The witness's testimony contradicts the physical evidence.

words.definitionEn: not varying; the same in all cases
words.example: The company maintains a uniform policy across all branches.

words.definitionEn: showing a great deal of variety; very different
words.example: The student body is diverse, with students from over 50 countries.

words.definitionEn: similar in nature or character
words.example: This approach is akin to the method used in the previous study.

words.definitionEn: relating to or based on comparison
words.example: A comparative analysis of the two economic systems revealed key differences.

words.definitionEn: to reflect or resemble closely
words.example: The trends in consumer behavior mirror those observed in the last decade.

words.definitionEn: in disagreement; incompatible
words.example: The two parties hold conflicting views on tax reform.

words.definitionEn: the state of having two opposite or contradictory aspects
words.example: The polarity of opinions on the issue has made consensus difficult.

words.definitionEn: the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other
words.example: The symmetry of the building's design is aesthetically pleasing.

words.definitionEn: lack of symmetry or equality
words.example: The asymmetry in the distribution of wealth is a growing concern.

words.definitionEn: the state of being similar to someone or something
words.example: There is a strong resemblance between the two paintings.

words.definitionEn: the act of distinguishing or showing difference
words.example: The differentiation of products is essential for market segmentation.

words.definitionEn: mutually opposed or inconsistent
words.example: The evidence presented is contradictory and requires further investigation.

words.definitionEn: being the same in quantity, size, degree, or value
words.example: All participants were treated as equal under the study protocol.

words.definitionEn: lack of equality or fairness
words.example: Income inequality has been linked to social unrest.

words.definitionEn: to show or establish a connection between things
words.example: We need to relate these findings to the broader context.

words.definitionEn: a connection or relationship between things
words.example: There is a well-documented association between diet and health.

words.definitionEn: a form or version that differs from others
words.example: This is a new variant of the virus that shows different symptoms.

words.definitionEn: to recognize a distinction or difference
words.example: The ability to discriminate between subtle differences is important.

words.definitionEn: the act of examining similarities and differences
words.example: A comparison of the two methods indicates that Method A is more efficient.
